lines.text: Linear algebra in the browser, written in Rust. That's the pitch behind a repo of Antoine's called Dimension.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: WebAssembly. The heart of the repo is a Rust crate called mathlib, and it ships with WebAssembly demos so you can try it on a web page.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Dense and sparse linear algebra, matrix decompositions, 3D math, clustering, graph algorithms and transforms. It also has optional SIMD and GPU features if you want more speed.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Right, and the Dimension repo wraps it with kinematics, physics, rendering experiments and documentation. To try it, you build and test from the mathlib folder with cargo. The full page links the repo, the crate docs and the architecture notes.
